title: Grade 9 How Does Priestley Present Ideas About Power in An Inspector Calls
author: Dominic Salles
summary: In this follow-up to a grade 7 essay post, Dominic Salles argues that GCSE English literature essay grades track countable features rather than a mysterious quality. He counts quotations, methods, society-related words, the word patriarchal, explanations and total words, and reports that grade 7 essays average about 21 explanations, 643 words and 9 quotes while higher grades need more of each. Writing about society and patriarchy matters because it pushes students to write about the writer's ideas, which is where top grades sit. He adds a new idea that has no number: treating characters as constructs, such as Eva Smith who represents working-class women and the exploitation of women under patriarchal control. His central claim is that quality equals quantity, because the quality of an essay is the quality of its proof and explanations, so the more evidence and explanation a student produces, the harder it is for an examiner to deny a higher band. He cites examiners' objection that basic ideas do not improve by multiplying and rejects it as describing a pretend student, not a real one.
points: Salles claims that essay grades follow countable features: quotes, methods, explanations, society references, patriarchal references and total word count.
Words matter because they carry explanations and proof; he puts grade 4 near 400 words, grade 7 near 700 and grade 9 near 900.
Writing about society and patriarchy forces students to address the writer's ideas, where the top mark bands sit.
Treating characters as constructs, for example Eva Smith as a symbol of exploited working-class women, is a high-value idea students can grasp but teachers rarely teach.
He argues that quality is not a separate skill from quantity but the quality of the proof and argument, so teaching students to write more evidence-based explanation raises grades.
quotes: The more quotes you bring to your essay, the more evidence you are using in support of your argument. So your argument becomes more convincing, and gets a higher grade.

Every student can understand the idea of a patriarchal society. Nearly every student can understand that characters and events can be chosen by the writer to represent something about the lives of women in a society controlled by men.

This idea is that characters are like real people, sure, but they are also created in order to represent ideas, or to symbolise aspects of society. Examiners call this treating the character as a CONSTRUCT.

Every time you explain an idea or an interpretation, you are building a more convincing argument. You are like a lawyer arguing why someone his guilty or innocent - the more proof you have, the better your case.

If two students know the same amount of stuff about the text, the one who writes more will get a higher grade. That is why grade 4 is about 400 words, grade 7 is about 700 words and grade 9 is about 900 words.
But that is also wrong. The quality of your essay is the quality of your proof and explanations about that proof - it is the quality of your argument.
The more you write about the author’s ideas, the more impossible it is for an examiner to say you don’t have at least “clear understanding”.
